## Purpose

The `maint-*` commands fan one action out over every subproject the scan discovered, and a `*Record` is what one subproject's turn produced. It carries the command VERBATIM alongside the verdict, so the report is reproducible by hand — an operator reading `{"subproject":"apps/cli","command":"cargo fetch","ok":false}` knows exactly what to re-run. A dry run still produces a full record with `duration_ms: 0`, which makes the preview and the real run the same document shape and lets a caller diff them. The record never decides anything: the kind→command mapping is a separate pure function, tested on its own.

## Convention

Folder: apps/rt/src/commands/maint/** · Extension: .rs · Files of this role in this subproject: 2

Beyond the census facts, what both exemplars show:

- **Name and place.** `<Verb>Record` (`InstallRecord`, `ValidateRecord`), declared after the `*Opts` struct and immediately before the `*Report` that holds it.
- **Derives and visibility.** `#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]` and `pub(crate)`, with every field `pub`. One `///` line introduces it ("One subproject install result.").
- **Fields, in this order.** `subproject: String` (the project's `dir`, falling back to its `name`), `command: String` (`format!("{bin} {}", args.join(" "))`), `ok: bool`, `duration_ms: u64`.
- **Paired report.** `pub(crate) struct Maint<X>Report { pub dry_run: bool, [pub overall: &'static str,] pub <plural>: Vec<XRecord> }`, also `#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]`, doc'd `/// JSON report.`. `maint_validate` adds `overall` with the closed set `"skip"` (no projects at all) / `"pass"` / `"fail"`.
- **Command table.** `#[must_use] pub(crate) fn <verb>_command(kind: &str) -> Option<(&'static str, Vec<&'static str>)>`, matching on `kind.to_ascii_lowercase()` from grain's manifest, accepting common stack aliases, and returning `None` for an unknown stack — that subproject is skipped, not recorded as a failure.
- **Builder.** A private `fn <verb>_all(dry_run: bool) -> Maint<X>Report` iterating `mustard_core::read_projects(&model)` where `model` is `cwd/.claude/grain.model.json`; on `dry_run` it pushes the record and `continue`s before spawning; otherwise it times the run with `Instant` and sets `ok` from `matches!(result, Ok(ref o) if o.status.success())`.
- **Process spawn.** Always `mustard_core::platform::process::rtk_command(bin, &args).current_dir(&run_dir).output()` — never `Command::new` directly.
- **Entry.** `pub fn run(opts: Maint<X>Opts)` prints `serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report)` and then emits one economy operation event; sequential by design ("parallelism is left to the user — this is a maintenance helper, not a CI driver").
- **Tests.** `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` covering the command table (known stacks, unknown stack `None`, case-insensitivity), the dry-run zero-duration record, and the JSON field names.

## How to apply

Copy the pair: declare `<Verb>Record` then `Maint<X>Report` in the new `maint_<verb>.rs`, write the kind→command table as its own `#[must_use]` function, then the `<verb>_all(dry_run)` builder with the dry-run branch first, then the printing `run`. Register the subcommand the way the subproject guard requires (variant + arm in `commands/maint/cli.rs`, the locked list in `tests/run_command_surface.rs`, and a real caller).

Must not: report a subproject whose kind has no command as a failure; skip the record on a dry run; build the command string in two places; spawn without `rtk_command`; parallelise the fan-out.

## Examples

- Ref: apps/rt/src/commands/maint/maint_deps.rs — `InstallRecord` + `MaintDepsReport`, the `install_command` table, and the dry-run test asserting `duration_ms: 0`.
- Ref: apps/rt/src/commands/maint/maint_validate.rs — the same pair plus `overall`, including the `"skip"` early return when the model lists no projects.
